correctness.rationale: The proof concerns strictly positive external assets t*a with fixed liabilities normalized to one, outside obligations positive in each row, and marginal total gross payments at each fixed t. The capped clearing map is an order-preserving l1 contraction because max row sum of T is below one, so the solution is unique, continuous in inputs, and nondecreasing in t and injections. On each strict default-set interval the local gain equals the relevant coordinate of (I-T_DD)^(-1)1 and is zero off D. This follows by differentiating the affine restricted clearing system, with fully solvent payments unchanged by a sufficiently small nonnegative injection. For one or two banks the default sets are nested: there is at most a constant all-default ranking, then one remaining potential winner, then no strict winner. Ties and simultaneous exits do not allow strict reentry. In the witness the all-default branch first reaches p_3=1 at 42/95; with bank 3 fully paying, the two-bank default branch reaches p_2=1 at 126/61; with only bank 1 defaulting the payment is 7/10+t/20 until t=6. Endpoint inequalities and affine continuation verify the fixed-point conditions throughout the open intervals, using uniqueness. The exact gain comparisons are (416,374,342)/105, (55,70,0)/48 and (1,0,0), hence winners 1,2,1. Above t=6 all gains are zero; no strict winner is asserted at the breakpoints. The independent rational replay /workspace/branches/84a4b2c9-7df5-47cb-a03c-ad6b9877123c/rational_replay.py also checked the affine segments, switch identities, and injections of 1/1000 in each coordinate at t=1/4,1,3. The supplied verify.py was inspected, not executed; finite evidence checks the witness, not the universal lower bound.
